cu-porcellio-laevis.title: Dairy Cow / Milkback Isopod
cu-porcellio-laevis.summary: A big, bold black-and-white isopod and one of the classic cleanup-crew species. Dairy Cows eat a lot, process waste fast and breed quickly, and their size and calcium-rich shell mean they can double as an occasional feeder.
rows: Up to about 2 cm (0.8 in); one of the larger species
Heavy-duty cleanup of waste and decaying matter in bioactive enclosures; also an occasional supplemental feeder
Warm and humid; keep moist substrate with sphagnum moss and cork bark
About 64–79°F (18–26°C); ordinary room temperature works well. Avoid sustained heat above about 82°F (28°C)
Leaf litter and decaying wood plus regular protein (fish flakes or dried shrimp) and calcium (crushed eggshell or cuttlebone). Underfed on protein, they may turn cannibal
Fast, reliable breeder; a small group soon becomes a big colony
Larger tropical bioactive setups; culture in a ventilated tub at least shoebox size
Shy; mostly hidden by day and more active at night
notes: Keep different trade lines (Dairy Cow, Milk Back) in separate cultures; some may not interbreed.
warn: Isopods die if they dry out: keep part of the substrate moist at all times.

sources.name: Herpeton Academy – Porcellio laevis care guide

cu-porcellionides-pruinosus.title: Powder Isopod (Powder Blue / Powder Orange)
cu-porcellionides-pruinosus.summary: A small, fast, dusty-looking isopod that comes in blue-silver and orange color forms. Hardy, adaptable and very prolific, it's an excellent beginner cleanup crew for most terrarium setups.
rows: Very active cleanup crew that eats decaying organic matter and keeps enclosures clean
Prefers humidity; adapts to a wide range. Use moisture-retaining substrate in a mostly closed container
Decaying leaves and wood, plus some protein
Tropical to temperate (even semi-arid with a moist area); culture in a shoebox-size tub or larger with a loose lid
About 1 year in the wild; 2–3 years in captivity
Native to Europe; now found worldwide
notes: Soft-bodied and fast; not a species for handling.
Escape artists: keep the lid on.
warn: Isopods die if they dry out: keep part of the substrate moist at all times.

cu-trichorhina-tomentosa.title: Dwarf White Isopod
cu-trichorhina-tomentosa.summary: A tiny, all-white tropical isopod that lives mostly out of sight in the soil. Every adult can reproduce on its own (no males needed), so a few quickly become a working cleanup crew, ideal for small, humid terrariums and dart frog vivariums.
rows: Out-of-sight cleanup crew in the soil; good for small enclosures
High humidity: at least 50%, ideally 80%+, with moisture-retaining tropical substrate
Room temperature (about 70–80°F); breeds fastest in the 80s °F
All-female and reproduces asexually; numbers build quickly but tend to level off in small tanks
Small humid tropical terrariums and vivariums
Tropical Central America; now spread through the tropics
warn: Isopods die if they dry out: keep part of the substrate moist at all times.

cu-springtails.title: Springtail Culture
cu-springtails.summary: Tiny jumping soil animals that are the best natural mold control for a terrarium. They eat mold and decaying matter, help recycle nutrients for plants, and keep humid enclosures and isopod cultures cleaner.
rows: Mold control and waste breakdown in humid bioactive enclosures and isopod cultures
Need moist, humid conditions; escapees quickly dry out, so they don't infest the house
Mold, fungi and decaying organic matter; if supplementing, use only a pinch so leftovers don't rot
Closed or humid terrariums, vivariums and isopod cultures; not useful in dry succulent setups

cu-cubaris-murina.title: Papaya Isopod (Little Sea Isopod)
cu-cubaris-murina.summary: A small, domed pill isopod that rolls into a ball when disturbed. Papaya is a colorful captive morph of Cubaris murina (the "little sea" isopod), one of the more forgiving tropical display isopods. It needs leaf litter, a moist corner and calcium.
rows: Cleanup crew and display isopod for tropical bioactive setups
Keep about one-third of the substrate damp (not soggy) and the rest only lightly damp, with good ventilation; roughly 70–85% humidity. No water bowl
Leaf litter and soft rotting hardwood at all times; vegetables or isopod food once or twice a week and a little protein about weekly. Calcium (cuttlebone, oyster shell) always available
Females carry young in a pouch; about 15–35 young per brood
Starter colony of 20–30 in a ventilated box about 12 × 8 × 6 in with at least 2.5 in of leaf-rich substrate
Burrows and forages mostly after dark
warn: Isopods die if they dry out: keep part of the substrate moist at all times.

sources.name: Herpeton Academy – Cubaris murina care guide

bp-pilea-peperomioides.title: Chinese Money Plant
bp-pilea-peperomioides.summary: A compact, easy houseplant from the mountains of Yunnan, China, with round, coin-like leaves held on long stalks like little lily pads. It suits larger tropical terrariums with bright, indirect light and is pet-safe.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For planted terrariums, not for underwater use
Upright clumping perennial with round leaves up to 4 in across
Mid-ground or a focal plant in a larger tropical terrarium
Bright, indirect light (no harsh direct sun)
Light. A compact clump that adds offsets (pups) around its base
Offsets (pups) or stem cuttings, best in spring or early summer
Moist, well-drained mix; likes moderate to high humidity but tolerates average home humidity. Keep away from cold drafts and heat sources
Listed as pet friendly (safe for pets and children)

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Pilea peperomioides

bp-chamaedorea-elegans.title: Neanthe Bella (Parlor) Palm
bp-chamaedorea-elegans.summary: A small, slow-growing palm from Mexico and Central America and one of the toughest indoor palms, thriving in dim light and dry air. It adds height and a tropical look to large terrariums.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For planted terrariums, not for underwater use
Slender palm; each stem is single, but several are usually potted together
Background plant for tall tropical terrariums
Bright, indirect light; tolerates low light and deep shade
Usually 2–5 ft indoors; can reach 6–7 ft or more outdoors in warm climates
Moderate. A slow, clumping palm with a woody, rhizomatous base; repot only when needed
Well-drained soil; let it dry slightly between waterings. Grows best in evenly moist soil; overwatering is the main risk. Low to medium humidity is fine
Listed as non-toxic to cats and dogs; the fruit juice can irritate skin

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Chamaedorea elegans

bp-pilea-involucrata-moon-valley.title: Pilea 'Moon Valley' (Friendship Plant)
bp-pilea-involucrata-moon-valley.summary: A bushy, low, trailing tropical plant with deeply quilted, chartreuse-green leaves and bronze veins that look like the surface of the moon. It loves warmth and humidity, stays compact and is a classic terrarium plant.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For planted terrariums, not for underwater use
Bushy, creeping and trailing perennial with textured leaves
Foreground or mid-ground ground cover in humid tropical terrariums
Bright, indirect light to dappled shade
Light. A compact, shallow-rooted creeper that spreads by trailing stems
Stem cuttings or division; pinch tips to keep it compact
Keep evenly moist (less in winter) in a peaty, well-drained mix with high humidity
Listed as non-toxic to cats and dogs

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Pilea involucrata

bp-fittonia-albivenis.title: Pink Fittonia (Nerve Plant)
bp-fittonia-albivenis.summary: A small, creeping ground cover from South American rainforests with leaves netted in pink, red or white veins. It's a favorite for humid terrariums and vivariums; it wilts dramatically if it dries out but perks up after watering.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For planted terrariums, not for underwater use
Foreground ground cover in small humid terrariums, frog vivariums and tropical gecko setups
Bright to medium indirect light; no direct sun
Light. Shallow roots; the creeping stems root as they spread
Stem cuttings root easily when a node touches damp soil
Keep moist with high humidity, but don't let leaves stay wet all day; give ventilation. Leaves shrivel in dry air, drafts or direct sun
Generally treated as non-toxic, but it is not a food plant for reptiles
Rainforests of Bolivia, northern Brazil, Colombia, Peru and Venezuela
notes: Don't plant it where heavy or digging animals will crush it.

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Fittonia albivenis

bp-peperomia-prostrata.title: String of Turtles
bp-peperomia-prostrata.summary: A delicate, slow-growing trailing plant from Ecuador with tiny, round, succulent leaves patterned like little turtle shells. It's perfect for small terrariums and hanging displays and is not aggressive.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For planted terrariums, not for underwater use
Trailing over hardscape or in the foreground of small terrariums
Bright, indirect light; tolerates lower light with duller color
Light. Small root system; does well pot-bound and is not aggressive
Evenly moist but never soggy (easily overwatered); average to higher humidity
Listed as non-toxic to cats and dogs

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Peperomia prostrata

bp-pilea-cadierei.title: Aluminum Plant
bp-pilea-cadierei.summary: An upright, bushy tropical plant from China and Vietnam whose dark green leaves look splashed with silver paint. It likes warmth, humidity and bright indirect light, and stays a compact clump that's easy to refresh from cuttings.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For planted terrariums, not for underwater use
Mid-ground plant in humid tropical terrariums
Bright, indirect light to shade; avoid full sun
Usually about 9–12 in indoors (up to 2 ft)
Moderate. Forms underground rhizomes and spreads into a dense clump
Stem cuttings in early spring (young plants have the best foliage); pinch tips to keep it compact
Moderate watering in the growing season, less in fall and winter; high humidity

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Pilea cadierei

bp-dionaea-muscipula.title: Venus Flytrap
bp-dionaea-muscipula.summary: The famous snap-trap carnivorous plant, native only to the coastal bogs of North and South Carolina. It needs bright sun, constantly wet, nutrient-poor soil and pure water, and it naturally goes dormant in winter.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For planted terrariums, not for underwater use
Small clumping carnivorous rosette with hinged traps
Bog-style or carnivorous plant setups with strong light; not a typical humid-jungle terrarium plant
Full sun to partial shade (at least several hours of direct light)
Keep constantly wet in pure sphagnum or peat mixed with sand or vermiculite; use rainwater or distilled water only (tap or hard water can kill it). Never fertilize; high humidity
Listed as non-toxic to cats and dogs
Coastal bogs of North and South Carolina, USA
notes: Traps close when an insect touches two of the trigger hairs; it digests the prey and reopens.
Protected in the wild; all plants sold are nursery-propagated.
warn: Use only rainwater or distilled water and never fertilizer.

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Dionaea muscipula

bp-strobilanthes-alternata-exotica.title: Purple Waffle Plant
bp-strobilanthes-alternata-exotica.summary: A low, spreading tropical plant with glossy, puckered purple-green leaves (red underneath) that look like they've been pressed in a waffle iron. It makes colorful ground cover in warm, humid terrariums and is listed as non-toxic to cats and dogs.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For planted terrariums, not for underwater use
Low, spreading herbaceous perennial (ground cover) with small white flowers
Foreground ground cover or a trailing plant in tropical terrariums
Very bright but indirect light. Too little dulls the purple color and harsh sun bleaches it
About 6–9 in tall, spreading 12–18 in wide
Moderate. A creeping ground cover that spreads sideways
Keep above 60°F (16°C); it dies below about 50°F (10°C)
Keep the soil moist but well-drained, in a rich, organic mix. Water when the top 1/2 in of soil is dry; let it get a little drier (never bone-dry) during a winter rest
Listed as non-toxic for cats, dogs and horses
notes: Older plants get leggy and lose their lower leaves and color; pinch or replace them.

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Strobilanthes alternata 'Exotica'
NYBG Plant Information – Purple waffle plant care

cu-isopods-mixed.title: Isopods (morph and mixed cultures)
cu-isopods-mixed.summary: Isopods (woodlice) are small land crustaceans that eat decaying leaves, wood and waste, keeping bioactive enclosures clean. This listing is a named color morph or a mix, sold without a species name; the care below is common to the popular hobby isopods.
rows: Most hobby isopods are about 0.5–2 cm
Cleanup crew: break down droppings, shed skin, leftover food and leaf litter in bioactive setups; can also be an occasional snack for small insect-eaters
They breathe through gill-like organs and dry out easily: keep part of the substrate damp (moss or a moist corner) and the rest only lightly moist, with some airflow. No water bowl needed
Room temperature, about 70–80°F (21–27°C); avoid sustained heat above about 82°F (28°C)

Leaf litter and soft rotting hardwood at all times, plus a little protein (fish flakes, dried shrimp) and a calcium source (cuttlebone, crushed eggshell). Vegetables as an occasional extra; remove moldy leftovers
Females carry their young in a pouch; most hobby species breed readily once settled
Humid tropical and temperate bioactive terrariums; culture in a shoebox-size or larger tub with leaf-rich substrate
Mostly hide by day and forage after dark
notes: Keep the lid on; many isopods climb and escape.
Mixing species in one culture can let one outcompete the others; some larger isopods will eat smaller ones.

sources.name: Herpeton Academy – Cubaris murina care guide

bp-echeveria-assorted.title: Echeveria (assorted)
bp-echeveria-assorted.summary: Echeverias are rosette-forming succulents from dry country between Texas and Argentina, with thick, fleshy leaves in grey, blue-green and other colors. They suit bright, dry (desert) setups and need little water.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For terrariums, not for underwater use
Low succulent rosette; many species and hybrids
Foreground or rock ledges in a dry, desert-style terrarium
Full sun to part sun; color is best in strong light
Light. A small rosette that adds offsets at its base
Offsets, beheaded crowns or single leaves laid on soil
Sparing: very well-drained sandy mix; needs little water
notes: Remove withered lower leaves, which can harbor disease.

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Echeveria

bp-sedum-assorted.title: Sedum / Stonecrop (assorted)
bp-sedum-assorted.summary: Sedums are tough succulent ground covers with fleshy leaves that sprawl over rocks and root as they spread. Easy in bright, dry terrariums with gritty soil.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For terrariums, not for underwater use
Ground cover or rock ledges in a dry terrarium
Bright direct light (sun to part sun or a grow light)
About 3 in to 2 ft, depending on species
Moderate. Low types spread by rooting stems
Fallen leaves, leaf cuttings or seed
Coarse, well-drained (cactus-type) mix; drought tolerant; avoid wet, poorly drained soil
notes: Leaves drop off easily, but fallen leaves root into new plants.

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Sedum

bp-haworthia-assorted.title: Haworthia (assorted)
bp-haworthia-assorted.summary: Haworthias are small South African succulents that form clumping rosettes of thick, often striped or "windowed" leaves. Easy and low-maintenance, they suit small desert terrariums.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For terrariums, not for underwater use
Bright indirect light to sun (tolerates some low light); best color in good light
Light. A compact clump that adds offsets
Division of offsets or leaf cuttings
Well-drained mix; let it dry between waterings; average home humidity is fine
notes: Many plants sold as Haworthia are now placed in Haworthiopsis or Tulista.

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Haworthia

bp-hoya-assorted.title: Hoya / Wax Plant (assorted)
bp-hoya-assorted.summary: Hoyas are climbing, epiphytic vines from tropical Asia and the western Pacific with thick, waxy leaves and often fragrant flowers. Easy to grow if the roots never stay soggy.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For terrariums, not for underwater use
Climbing a background, branch or pole in a tropical terrarium
Bright light or dappled shade; not full sun all day
Light. Epiphytic roots; needs a free-draining mix
Free-draining organic mix that dries between waterings; does not tolerate soggy roots
Tropical and subtropical Asia and western Pacific islands
notes: Grows best with something to climb.
Watch for mealybugs, aphids and spider mites.

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Hoya

bp-tillandsia-assorted.title: Air Plant (Tillandsia, assorted)
bp-tillandsia-assorted.summary: Air plants are rosette bromeliads that grow on branches and rocks instead of in soil, taking water and nutrients through silvery scales on their leaves. Easy, but they need bright light and regular soaking.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For terrariums, not for underwater use
Mounted on wood, cork or rock in a terrarium
High light: a bright window or grow light (needed for flowering)
None. Only small holdfast roots for grip; leaves take up water
Soak or rinse the whole plant at least once a week
Southern USA, Mexico and South America
notes: Do not bury it in substrate.

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Tillandsia

bp-peperomia-assorted.title: Peperomia (assorted)
bp-peperomia-assorted.summary: Peperomias are small, slow-growing tropical houseplants with fleshy, often patterned leaves. Easy and compact, they suit tropical terrariums with bright, indirect light.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For terrariums, not for underwater use
Small upright, trailing or climbing perennial
Foreground or mid-ground in a tropical terrarium; trailing types for ledges
Bright indirect light; tolerates low light
Light. Compact, slow growth; seldom needs repotting
Leaf or stem cuttings, or division
Moist, well-drained mix; do not overwater; average to higher humidity; keep away from cold drafts
Tropical and subtropical Americas, Africa, Southeast Asia and Australia

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Peperomia

bp-begonia-assorted.title: Begonia (assorted)
bp-begonia-assorted.summary: Begonias are forest-floor plants from the tropics with showy, often asymmetrical leaves in many colors and textures. They like shade, rich soil and moisture, making them good tropical terrarium plants.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For terrariums, not for underwater use
Clumping or upright perennial; foliage and flowering types
Mid-ground in a shaded tropical terrarium
Moist but well-drained, rich organic mix
Tropics and subtropics of the Americas, Africa and Asia
warn: Listed as a problem for cats, and can cause contact dermatitis.

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Begonia

bp-calathea-assorted.title: Calathea / Goeppertia (assorted)
bp-calathea-assorted.summary: Calatheas (now mostly Goeppertia) are prayer-plant relatives from Central and South America grown for their patterned leaves, which fold up at night. They want warmth, humidity and soft water.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For terrariums, not for underwater use
Mid-ground or background in a humid tropical terrarium
About 9 in to 3 ft, depending on species
Moist, rich, well-drained mix (not soggy); high humidity; use distilled or rain water, since tap water can damage leaves
notes: Feed only in the growing season, at half strength.

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Goeppertia

bp-maranta-leuconeura.title: Prayer Plant (Maranta)
bp-maranta-leuconeura.summary: The prayer plant has patterned leaves with red, fishbone-like veins that lie flat by day and fold upward at night. A low, spreading tropical plant that needs humidity and indirect light.
rows: On land (terrestrial). For terrariums, not for underwater use
Ground cover or foreground in a humid tropical terrarium
Bright indirect to low-medium light; direct sun bleaches the leaves
About 6–12 in tall, up to 2 ft wide
Keep evenly moist in the growing season, a little drier in winter; needs high humidity
warn: Sensitive to cold drafts, fluoride and over-fertilizing (leaf burn).

sources.name: NC State Extension Plant Toolbox – Maranta leuconeura
